resources.name: jmdict-eng
resources.description: The JMdict Japanese-English dictionary, as scriptin's JSON rebuild of the EDRDG XML. Every headword, reading, sense and gloss the app shows comes from here — it is the spine the rest of these resources annotate.
resources.provenance: scriptin/jmdict-simplified release asset; local extracted file hash pinned

resources.name: extras
resources.description: Hand-written entries for words JMdict does not carry, mostly katakana fragments (ユア) the segmenter needs in order to split compounds. Merged into the same tables as JMdict so lookup and segmentation cannot tell them apart.
resources.provenance: project-maintained supplemental dictionary entries

resources.name: jpdb-frequency-kana
resources.description: Word-frequency ranks measured over a large corpus of Japanese media, keyed by kana spelling. Drives the Common/Rare tier badge and orders homographs so the reading a learner will actually meet is the one shown first.
resources.provenance: JPDB v2.2 frequency dictionary by Kuuuube (yomitan-permalink release); generate_db.py downloads the zip and extracts term_meta_bank_1.json to Resources/jpdb-frequency-kana-2.2.json

resources.name: wordfreq
resources.description: Python package giving a Zipf frequency for any Japanese string. It is the only frequency source covering words usually written in kana (この, する, こと), which JPDB's kana ranks miss; without it those everyday words rank as Rare, so the build hard-fails rather than ship that silently.
resources.provenance: Python package; install with: pip install wordfreq mecab-python3 ipadic

resources.name: kanjidic2-all
resources.description: Per-character kanji data: readings, meanings, stroke counts, grade and JLPT level. Backs the Kanji breakdown on a word's detail screen and the standalone kanji browser.
resources.provenance: scriptin/jmdict-simplified kanjidic2-all release asset; generate_db.py downloads the zip and extracts kanjidic2-all-3.6.2.json to Resources/kanjidic2-all.json

resources.name: pitch-accent
resources.description: Accent type and mora count per word, derived from UniDic's kana-accent lexicon. Shows where the pitch drop falls — something printed dictionaries usually omit even though it changes how a word is pronounced.
resources.provenance: Derived in-process by generate_db.py from unidic-kana-accent-src: lex.csv rows with an accent value; word = surface, kana = base-form pronunciation, kind = second POS field (first if "*"), accent = first accent type, morae = kana minus small kana; rows with accent > morae dropped; duplicates dropped keeping file order. sha256 is the canonical TSV written by `generate_db.py --emit-derived DIR` (CRLF, header row) — verified byte-identical to the file this replaced.
resources.sha256Scheme: file: SHA-256 of pitch-accent.tsv as written by generate_db.py --emit-derived

resources.name: sentence-pairs
resources.description: Aligned Japanese/English sentence pairs from Tatoeba. Supplies the examples under a sense so a gloss is backed by real usage instead of a bare translation.
resources.provenance: Derived in-process by generate_db.py from the Tatoeba exports: every link between a Japanese and an English sentence, sorted by (ja_id, en_id); tab-split, never CSV-unquoted. Tatoeba re-exports weekly, so the output (and its hash) changes over time — no hash pinned. Replaces the hand-built 2026-01-20 TSV, whose script was lost and which had corrupted ~2,100 English sentences that begin with a quotation mark.

resources.name: jlpt-vocab
resources.description: Which JLPT level (N5-N1) each word sits at. Fills the level badge on a word and lets learners filter and sort their study lists by exam level.
resources.provenance: Derived in-process by generate_db.py from jlpt-vocab-source (rows with a non-blank surface and level 1-5). sha256 is the canonical TSV written by `generate_db.py --emit-derived DIR` — verified byte-identical to the file this replaced. Consumed by import_jlpt_levels to populate entry_jlpt_level. Replaces scripts/build_jlpt_vocab_tsv.py.
resources.sha256Scheme: file: SHA-256 of jlpt-vocab.tsv as written by generate_db.py --emit-derived

resources.name: radkfile2
resources.description: Radical-to-kanji index: which characters contain a given radical. Powers radical lookup, the way to find a kanji you can neither read nor type.
resources.provenance: EDRDG RADKFILE2 (extended radical set). License: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group). generate_db.py downloads kradzip.zip, extracts the radkfile2 member (a zip member, EUC-JP) and converts it to UTF-8 as Resources/radkfile2.utf8

resources.name: kradfile2
resources.description: The inverse index, kanji to its component radicals. Shows what a character is built from, and narrows the radical picker as components are chosen.
resources.provenance: EDRDG KRADFILE2 (extended radical set). License: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group). generate_db.py downloads kradzip.zip, extracts the kradfile2 member (a zip member, EUC-JP) and converts it to UTF-8 as Resources/kradfile2.utf8

resources.name: handwriting-ja
resources.description: Zinnia/Tegaki stroke-based recognition model, letting users draw a kanji they cannot type. ~25MB and LGPL, so it is fetched per machine rather than committed.
resources.provenance: Tegaki-Zinnia Japanese handwriting recognition model (~25MB). Consumed by the Zinnia recognizer via the Packages/zinnia-swift local Swift package (feat/handwriting branch). License: LGPL — see the Tegaki project for redistribution terms. Download the Japanese model from https://tegaki.github.io and save as Resources/handwriting-ja.model.

resources.name: kanjivg
resources.description: Per-character stroke paths in drawing order. Drives the animated stroke-order diagrams, and is the only source here that knows how a character is written rather than what it means.
resources.provenance: KanjiVG (Kanji Vector Graphics) by Ulrich Apel et al., release r20250816 single-file XML (kanjivg-20250816.xml.gz). License: CC BY-SA 3.0. generate_db.py downloads the gzip and decompresses it to Resources/kanjivg.xml. (An earlier version of this entry pointed at the r20220427 -main.zip, which holds per-character SVGs, not the XML the builder reads.)

resources.name: dictionary
resources.description: The SQLite database the app actually queries — every resource below marked feedsDictionary compiled into a single file by generate_db.py. Downloaded on first launch instead of bundled, because at ~350MB it would otherwise dominate the install.
resources.provenance: Generated by generate_db.py from every manifest entry with feedsDictionary=true (see the top-level "regeneration" and "tools" blocks). Neither bundled into Kioku.app nor committed to git: the local Resources/dictionary.sqlite is downloaded from the release url above by scripts/ensure_dictionary.sh (for tests, CI, and generate_db.py's own staleness check), and at runtime DictionaryDownloadManager fetches that same asset into Application Support on first launch, verified against the sha256 above. To republish after a rebuild with meaningfully different content: run generate_db.py, bump the tag, recompute the sha256 both here and in DictionaryDownloadManager.releaseTag/expectedSHA256, then run scripts/publish_dictionary_release.sh locally. There is no CI automation for this — generate_db.py's upstream inputs are gitignored and exist only on whichever machine ran the generator.

resources.name: mecab-ipadic-matrix
resources.description: IPADIC's bigram connection-cost matrix — the cost of following one word class with another. The default trie segmenter's Viterbi scorer reads it to choose between competing splits, so it is the one piece of MeCab data committed directly (3.5MB) rather than fetched: a fresh clone would otherwise segment worse with no sign anything was missing.
resources.provenance: IPADIC 2.7.0-20070801 bigram connection-cost matrix, byte-identical to the PyPI `ipadic` package (source: github.com/polm/ipadic-py). Only piece of MeCab data the DEFAULT trie segmenter needs — IPADicMatrix.swift feeds it into the Viterbi scorer's node-transition costs. Small enough (3.5MB) to commit directly (see .gitignore's exception carve-out) so a fresh clone's default configuration isn't silently degraded, unlike the rest of MeCab's data below.

resources.name: mecab-ipadic-full
resources.description: The complete IPADIC dictionary, for the optional MeCab segmentation backend. Reachable only via Settings > Segmentation > Engine: MeCab; the app falls back to the trie segmenter when it is absent, so it is not checked in.
resources.sha256Scheme: tree: SHA-256 of sorted "relative/path<TAB>file-sha256" lines joined by newlines with a trailing newline, excluding .DS_Store
resources.provenance: Full IPADIC 2.7.0-20070801 (sys.dic + unk.dic + char.bin + dicrc, ~49.5MB) — byte-identical to the PyPI `ipadic` package for char.bin/dicrc/matrix.bin; sys.dic/unk.dic differ by build/version of the same standard vocabulary (see repo investigation notes). Only needed for the opt-in Settings → Segmentation → Engine: MeCab backend (its default dictionary). Not required: the app falls back to the trie segmenter if these files are absent (MeCabSegmenter's failable init). Not checked in — obtain via `pip install ipadic` (extracts to the package's dicdir) or an equivalent mecab-ipadic 2.7.0 distribution, and copy sys.dic/unk.dic/char.bin/dicrc into Resources/MeCab/ipadic/.

resources.name: mecab-unidic
resources.description: UniDic for the MeCab backend — an alternative to IPADIC with finer-grained parts of speech. Two settings changes past the default and ~196MB, so it is deliberately kept outside the Resources/MeCab/ folder Xcode bundles wholesale, and ships to nobody.
resources.deletedLocally: 2026-08-09 — removed from disk to reclaim 196MB; was confirmed unused (not referenced by Kioku.xcodeproj's build phases, not read by SegmenterBackend.swift or any other Swift source by path). Verified the restore link below is still live and version-matches this entry (same cwj/2.1.2 directory the pitch-accent entry's unidic-mecab_kana-accent-2.1.2_src.zip already comes from) before deleting.
resources.provenance: UniDic-MeCab (~196MB) — the largest single resource in the project, and NOT bundled into the app: it lives outside Resources/MeCab/ (which Xcode bundles wholesale as a folder reference) specifically so it's excluded from the shipped app. Reachable only via Settings → Segmentation → Engine: MeCab, then Dictionary: UniDic — two manual changes past the trie default, exercised by essentially no users. Sourced from the NINJAL UniDic archive (same host family as this manifest's pitch-accent entry). To restore: download the url above (unidic-mecab-2.1.2_bin.zip, ~44MB — the pre-built binary distribution, not the larger _src.zip), extract sys.dic/unk.dic/char.bin/dicrc/matrix.bin into Resources/MeCab-unidic-optional/unidic/, verify each against perFileSHA256BeforeDeletion above, then re-add that path as a bundled Resources build-phase entry in Kioku.xcodeproj if you want it shipped again.

resources.name: unidic-kana-accent-src
resources.description: The UniDic source archive the pitch-accent table is derived from. Pinned as its own entry so the derivation's input is reproducible rather than implied.
resources.provenance: UniDic-MeCab kana-accent 2.1.2 source archive (NINJAL). sha256 is the hash of the lex.csv member; fetch.archiveSha256 is the zip. Input to derive_pitch_accent_rows in generate_db.py.

resources.name: tatoeba-jpn-sentences
resources.description: Tatoeba's Japanese sentence export — the Japanese half of the example-sentence pairs.
resources.provenance: Tatoeba per-language export of Japanese sentences (id, language, text). Re-exported weekly, so no hash is pinned. License: CC BY 2.0 FR. Input to derive_sentence_pairs_rows.

resources.name: tatoeba-eng-sentences
resources.description: Tatoeba's English sentence export — the English half of the example-sentence pairs.
resources.provenance: Tatoeba per-language export of English sentences (id, language, text). Re-exported weekly, so no hash is pinned. License: CC BY 2.0 FR. Input to derive_sentence_pairs_rows.

resources.name: tatoeba-links
resources.description: Tatoeba's table of which sentence translates which, the join that turns the two exports above into aligned pairs. All languages and ~150MB, so it is streamed out of the archive rather than unpacked.
resources.provenance: Tatoeba sentence-link table (id, translation id; both directions), all languages, ~150MB. Re-exported weekly, so no hash is pinned. Input to derive_sentence_pairs_rows.

resources.name: jlpt-vocab-source
resources.description: Pinned CSV mirror of Jonathan Waller's JLPT vocabulary lists — the raw input the jlpt-vocab table is derived from.
resources.provenance: Cleaned CSV mirror (Kanji,Reading,Level) of Jonathan Waller's JLPT lists (https://www.tanos.co.uk/jlpt/, CC BY, unofficial estimates) from Bluskyo/JLPT_Vocabulary (MIT), pinned to commit d29a678. Input to derive_jlpt_vocab_rows.

resources.name: opencc-jp-shinjitai
resources.description: Modern-to-old-form (shinjitai/kyujitai) kanji correspondences. Generates KyujitaiTable.swift so a word written in prewar forms (國 for 国) still finds its entry. Feeds the app directly; generate_db.py never reads it.
resources.provenance: OpenCC (BYVoid/OpenCC, Apache-2.0) data/dictionary/JPShinjitaiCharacters.txt pinned to commit 6aa8c54: shinjitai <-> old-form (kyujitai / variant) kanji correspondences built from the Jouyou kanji table, the Jinmeiyou variant table and 22 shinjitai from the Hyougai kanji character-shape table. Input to scripts/generate_kyujitai_table.py, which writes Kioku/Dictionary/KyujitaiTable.swift (the table KyujitaiNormalizer applies in the trie and in dictionary lookup). Not used by generate_db.py.

tools.note: wordfreq supplies wordfreq_zipf; the mecab CLI plus mecab-ipadic supplies the IPADic context IDs. generate_db.py fails fast if either is missing.

options.--offline: never download; fail if a cached archive is missing
options.--sources-only: fetch and verify every source, then exit
options.--emit-derived DIR: write the derived TSVs (whose sha256 values are recorded here) to DIR, then exit

regeneration.cache: ~/Projects/kioku-source-cache, outside the checkout so it survives disposable worktrees; override with KIOKU_SOURCE_CACHE
regeneration.reproducibility: Direct inputs and the pitch-accent / jlpt-vocab derivations are byte-verified against the sha256 values recorded here. Tatoeba entries are marked rolling, so sentence_pairs content tracks Tatoeba's current export; everything else in the database is deterministic from the pinned inputs.
regeneration.publishing: After a rebuild changes the database, bump the release tag, recompute the dictionary sha256 here and in DictionaryDownloadManager.swift, and run scripts/publish_dictionary_release.sh.
